paragraphs.title: Gathering and Remembrance of the Fathers

easy.question: Who gathered all the tribes of Israel in verse 1?
answers: Joshua
Moses
Aaron
easy.explanation: The verse opens 'And Joshua gathered' — Joshua is the one who gathered the people.

easy.question: Where did Joshua gather all the tribes of Israel in verse 1?
answers: Bethel
Shechem
Shiloh
easy.explanation: Verse 1 states that he gathered them to Shechem.

easy.question: Who were called and set 'before God' in verse 1?
answers: Only the common people
Only the children and youth
The elders of the people, their leaders, judges and officers
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly lists the elders of Israel, their heads, judges and officers as those presented before God.

medium.question: What does the phrase 'dwelt on the other side of the flood' mean in this context?
answers: Along the river bank
On the far side of the river/flood
In the middle of the river
medium.explanation: In context it refers to dwelling on the far side of the river (traditionally Mesopotamia/Euphrates).

medium.question: Why does verse 2 say their fathers 'served other gods'?
answers: To show they were only nomads
To say they were subject to a foreign king
To emphasize they worshiped idols before God called the fathers
medium.explanation: The verse stresses that the fathers served other gods (idols), setting the background for entering covenant with the Lord.

medium.question: What is the first action described that God did for Abraham in verse 3?
answers: He took your father Abraham from the other side of the flood
He gave him Isaac
He led him into all the land of Canaan
medium.explanation: Verse 3 begins 'And I took your father Abraham from the other side of the flood' — the first action is taking Abraham from beyond the flood.

challenge.question: Why is it likely Joshua brought and set the elders and leaders 'before God' in the broader context?
answers: To anoint a new king for the people
To organize games and a festival
To confirm the covenant and remind them of their commitment to God
challenge.explanation: Presenting the elders and heads before the Lord implies a formal act of covenant renewal and a call to remember their obligations to God.

challenge.question: Which river is most likely meant by 'the flood' when referring to Abraham's origin?
answers: The Euphrates
The Jordan
The Nile
challenge.explanation: Tradition places Abraham's origins in Mesopotamia, associated with the Euphrates, so 'the flood' is commonly understood as the Euphrates.

challenge.question: Who is speaking in verse 3 when it says 'I took your father Abraham...'?
answers: Joshua
The LORD (God)
The people
challenge.explanation: Verse 2 begins 'Thus saith the Lord', so the 'I' in verse 3 continues God's speech, describing His actions regarding Abraham.

questions.question: Why is it likely Joshua brought and set the elders and leaders 'before God' in the broader context?
answers: To anoint a new king for the people
To organize games and a festival
To confirm the covenant and remind them of their commitment to God
questions.explanation: Presenting the elders and heads before the Lord implies a formal act of covenant renewal and a call to remember their obligations to God.

questions.question: Which river is most likely meant by 'the flood' when referring to Abraham's origin?
answers: The Euphrates
The Jordan
The Nile
questions.explanation: Tradition places Abraham's origins in Mesopotamia, associated with the Euphrates, so 'the flood' is commonly understood as the Euphrates.

questions.question: Who is speaking in verse 3 when it says 'I took your father Abraham...'?
answers: Joshua
The LORD (God)
The people
questions.explanation: Verse 2 begins 'Thus saith the Lord', so the 'I' in verse 3 continues God's speech, describing His actions regarding Abraham.

paragraphs.title: The Fathers' Story and the Exodus

easy.question: To whom did the Lord give Mount Seir to possess, according to verse 4?
answers: Jacob
Esau
The children of Jacob
easy.explanation: Verse 4 explicitly says Mount Seir was given to Esau to possess.

easy.question: Who did the LORD send to strike Egypt according to the passage?
answers: Moses and Aaron
Isaac and his sons
All the prophets
easy.explanation: Verse 5 says 'I sent Moses also and Aaron' — God sent Moses and Aaron.

easy.question: What happened to the Egyptians when they pursued after our fathers to the sea?
answers: The sea opened only
The sea weakened and stopped flowing
The sea covered them
easy.explanation: Verse 7 reports that God 'brought the sea upon them, and covered them' — the sea covered the Egyptians.

medium.question: What does the phrase 'he put darkness between you and the Egyptians' indicate?
answers: A period of sleep
A darkness that separated the Israelites from the Egyptians
A thick cloud of smoke
medium.explanation: It indicates God caused darkness to come between them so the Egyptians could not see the Israelites.

medium.question: What happened after the Egyptians pursued your fathers?
answers: The Egyptians conquered the sea
The people returned to Egypt
God brought the sea and covered the Egyptians
medium.explanation: The narrative says the Egyptians pursued, Israel cried out, and God brought the sea upon them, covering them.

medium.question: Which result is described as a lengthy period after the Exodus?
answers: They immediately returned to the fathers' land
They dwelt in the wilderness a long season
They remained on Mount Seir
medium.explanation: Verse 7 explicitly states they 'dwelt in the wilderness a long season' — a prolonged period in the wilderness.

challenge.question: What is the main purpose of mentioning what was given to Jacob and Esau at the start of this section?
answers: To show Jacob was wronged by God
To praise Esau particularly
To remind the people of God's acts and His connection to their ancestors
challenge.explanation: The passage opens with deeds God did for the fathers (giving them inheritances, sending deliverers) to emphasize God's ongoing care and relationship to the ancestors.

challenge.question: The reference to 'Mount Seir' primarily associates that area with which people?
answers: Canaan
Edom (descendants of Esau)
Moab
challenge.explanation: Mount Seir is traditionally associated with Edom and the descendants of Esau; the verse says it was given to Esau to possess.

challenge.question: What do the words 'chariots and horsemen' imply about the Egyptian forces that pursued them?
answers: War chariots and cavalry (vehicles and horse soldiers)
A fleet of ships
Only foot soldiers with no vehicles
challenge.explanation: 'Chariots' and 'horsemen' describe chariotry and mounted troops — a mechanized and mobile fighting force.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of mentioning what was given to Jacob and Esau at the start of this section?
answers: To show Jacob was wronged by God
To praise Esau particularly
To remind the people of God's acts and His connection to their ancestors
questions.explanation: The passage opens with deeds God did for the fathers (giving them inheritances, sending deliverers) to emphasize God's ongoing care and relationship to the ancestors.

questions.question: The reference to 'Mount Seir' primarily associates that area with which people?
answers: Canaan
Edom (descendants of Esau)
Moab
questions.explanation: Mount Seir is traditionally associated with Edom and the descendants of Esau; the verse says it was given to Esau to possess.

questions.question: What do the words 'chariots and horsemen' imply about the Egyptian forces that pursued them?
answers: War chariots and cavalry (vehicles and horse soldiers)
A fleet of ships
Only foot soldiers with no vehicles
questions.explanation: 'Chariots' and 'horsemen' describe chariotry and mounted troops — a mechanized and mobile fighting force.

paragraphs.title: Balaam and the Conquests of the Land

easy.question: Who arose and opposed Israel at the start of this section?
answers: Balaam son of Beor
Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab
The king of Jericho
easy.explanation: Verse 9 states 'Balak the son of Zippor king of Moab arose and warred against Israel' — Balak initiated opposition.

easy.question: What was Balak's mission according to verse 9?
answers: To curse Israel
To bless them
To marry a daughter of Israel
easy.explanation: Balak sent for Balaam to curse Israel — his intent was to have Israel cursed.

easy.question: Which crops are mentioned in verse 13 as things you did not plant but eat?
answers: Wheat and barley
Dates and palms
Vineyards and oliveyards
easy.explanation: Verse 13 names 'vineyards and oliveyards which ye planted not' as produce the people eat though they did not plant them.

medium.question: After you crossed the Jordan, which peoples fought against you according to the verse?
answers: The men of Jericho: the Amorite, the Perizzite, the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Girgashite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite
Moab and its tribes only
The Philistines only
medium.explanation: Verse 11 lists the peoples who fought at Jericho: the Amorites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hittites, Girgashites, Hivites and Jebusites.

medium.question: What does 'I sent the hornet before you' refer to in verse 12?
answers: A military commander
An attacking insect sent as a scourge
An angel of protection
medium.explanation: Here 'the hornet' refers to a stinging insect sent before you to drive out the inhabitants; the verse portrays it as God's means to expel them.

medium.question: Why does the text say 'the two kings of the Amorites were not by your sword nor by your bow'?
answers: To show the victory came from God not from Israel's weapons
To say the kings were captured in nets
To accuse the people of failing to use weapons
medium.explanation: The verse emphasizes the victory over the Amorite kings did not result from Israel's military arms but from God's intervention (including the hornet).

challenge.question: How, according to the verse, were the people of the land driven out before Israel — and what is the practical meaning of that?
answers: The LORD sent the hornet which drove them out, so they left the land
By an alliance with Moab that expelled the inhabitants
By natural diseases that killed them
challenge.explanation: Verse 12 says God sent the hornet and it drove them out before you — indicating God used agents under His control to remove the inhabitants, not solely Israel's military action.

challenge.question: What does the phrase in verse 13 'cities which ye built not, and ye dwell in them' imply about the people's situation in the land?
answers: They received towns and cultivated land already prepared — they inherited them rather than building or planting them
They must build and plant everything from scratch
They were punished for not farming the land
challenge.explanation: The passage says they dwelt in cities they had not built and ate from vineyards and oliveyards they did not plant — meaning they inherited ready resources.

challenge.question: Which people in the list of verse 11 is also known as the Jebusites, whose city later became associated with Jerusalem?
answers: The Jebusites
The Hivites
The Perizzites
challenge.explanation: The Jebusites (Jebusite) appear in the list and are elsewhere associated with the city later known as Jerusalem.

questions.question: How, according to the verse, were the people of the land driven out before Israel — and what is the practical meaning of that?
answers: The LORD sent the hornet which drove them out, so they left the land
By an alliance with Moab that expelled the inhabitants
By natural diseases that killed them
questions.explanation: Verse 12 says God sent the hornet and it drove them out before you — indicating God used agents under His control to remove the inhabitants, not solely Israel's military action.

questions.question: What does the phrase in verse 13 'cities which ye built not, and ye dwell in them' imply about the people's situation in the land?
answers: They received towns and cultivated land already prepared — they inherited them rather than building or planting them
They must build and plant everything from scratch
They were punished for not farming the land
questions.explanation: The passage says they dwelt in cities they had not built and ate from vineyards and oliveyards they did not plant — meaning they inherited ready resources.

questions.question: Which people in the list of verse 11 is also known as the Jebusites, whose city later became associated with Jerusalem?
answers: The Jebusites
The Hivites
The Perizzites
questions.explanation: The Jebusites (Jebusite) appear in the list and are elsewhere associated with the city later known as Jerusalem.

paragraphs.title: The Choice to Serve the Lord

easy.question: What does Joshua ask the people to do in verse 14?
answers: Fear the LORD and serve him in sincerity and in truth
Build altars for all gods
Return to serve in Egypt
easy.explanation: Joshua calls them to fear and serve the LORD 'in sincerity and in truth' — to serve God faithfully.

easy.question: How did the people respond to the proposal to serve the LORD (verse 16)?
answers: They chose to serve other gods
They refused to abandon the LORD
They asked for time to consider
easy.explanation: The people declare 'God forbid that we should forsake the LORD' — they insist they will not abandon Him.

easy.question: What reason do the people give for serving the LORD in verse 17?
answers: Because He gave them new laws
Because He sent them military aid
Because He brought them and their fathers out of Egypt and did great signs for them
easy.explanation: They cite the LORD bringing them out of Egypt and doing great signs as the reason they will serve Him.

medium.question: Why does Joshua ask 'Whom will ye serve?' in verse 15?
answers: To accuse the fathers of betrayal
To have them make a clear, immediate choice whom to serve
To invite foreigners to serve with them
medium.explanation: Joshua's question forces the people to make a conscious decision now about their loyalty.

medium.question: What does 'in sincerity' mean in the phrase 'serve him in sincerity and in truth'?
answers: Outward ritual only
With honesty and wholeheartedness
Under compulsion
medium.explanation: Here 'sincerity' means serving God honestly and with a genuine heart.

medium.question: Why does Joshua mention 'the gods which your fathers served on the other side of the flood and in Egypt' in verse 15?
answers: To urge them to sail back to those gods
To highlight the alternatives and force a clear choice between the LORD and other gods
To say those gods are superior
medium.explanation: Mentioning the foreign gods presents the options and makes the choice for the LORD deliberate and explicit.

challenge.question: What does the people's reply 'God forbid that we should forsake the LORD' suggest about the nature of their commitment (verse 16)?
answers: It signals internal division among the tribes
They are saying what Joshua wants to hear without real internal commitment
They are making a public, emphatic pledge to remain loyal to the LORD
challenge.explanation: The declaration is a strong public statement indicating they intend to remain faithful to the LORD.

challenge.question: How does verse 17 use memory of God's acts ('brought us out of Egypt', 'great signs') to persuade the people?
answers: To present a legal case against other gods
To show God's deeds as historical evidence of His claim to their loyalty
To make them feel guilty for past failings
challenge.explanation: The verse cites God's deliverance and signs as factual reasons to trust and serve Him.

challenge.question: What does the statement 'And the LORD drove out from before us all the people' (verse 18) indicate about Israel's possession of the land?
answers: The LORD was the agent who removed the peoples and allowed Israel to settle the land
The peoples left willingly before Israel arrived
The land was purchased through trade
challenge.explanation: The wording emphasizes that God drove out the inhabitants, framing Israel's settlement as enabled by the LORD's action.

questions.question: What does the people's reply 'God forbid that we should forsake the LORD' suggest about the nature of their commitment (verse 16)?
answers: It signals internal division among the tribes
They are saying what Joshua wants to hear without real internal commitment
They are making a public, emphatic pledge to remain loyal to the LORD
questions.explanation: The declaration is a strong public statement indicating they intend to remain faithful to the LORD.

questions.question: How does verse 17 use memory of God's acts ('brought us out of Egypt', 'great signs') to persuade the people?
answers: To present a legal case against other gods
To show God's deeds as historical evidence of His claim to their loyalty
To make them feel guilty for past failings
questions.explanation: The verse cites God's deliverance and signs as factual reasons to trust and serve Him.

questions.question: What does the statement 'And the LORD drove out from before us all the people' (verse 18) indicate about Israel's possession of the land?
answers: The LORD was the agent who removed the peoples and allowed Israel to settle the land
The peoples left willingly before Israel arrived
The land was purchased through trade
questions.explanation: The wording emphasizes that God drove out the inhabitants, framing Israel's settlement as enabled by the LORD's action.

easy.question: Why does Joshua say 'Ye cannot serve the LORD' in verse 19?
answers: Because the LORD is holy and jealous
Because the LORD is weak and cannot protect you
Because the LORD has forgotten you
easy.explanation: The verse says the LORD is holy and 'a jealous God' — meaning He will not tolerate disloyalty.

easy.question: How did the people respond to Joshua's warning in verse 21?
answers: They fled the camp
They offered a sacrifice to atone
They declared they would serve the LORD
easy.explanation: The people answered that they would serve the LORD.

easy.question: What did Joshua command the people to do in verse 23?
answers: Build a new altar
Put away the strange gods and incline their heart unto the LORD
Proclaim a holiday
easy.explanation: Joshua told them to remove foreign gods and turn their hearts to the LORD.

medium.question: What will happen if the people forsake the LORD and serve strange gods (verse 20)?
answers: The LORD will turn and do you hurt and consume you after He has done you good
The LORD will bless and multiply you
The LORD will ignore you and not remember you
medium.explanation: Verse 20 warns that if they forsake the LORD He will turn and harm them, even after great goodness.

medium.question: What does 'jealous' mean in the phrase 'he is a jealous God' (verse 19)?
answers: Generous and forgiving
Demands exclusive loyalty and will not tolerate unfaithfulness
Indifferent to human actions
medium.explanation: Here 'jealous' means God requires exclusive loyalty and will not endure idolatry.

medium.question: Why does Joshua ask the people to be 'witnesses' (verse 22)?
answers: So they would serve in court
So they would testify that they have chosen the LORD to serve
So they could appoint new judges
medium.explanation: Joshua asks for witnesses so the people publicly attest they have chosen the LORD and accept responsibility for that choice.

challenge.question: The people's double declarations (verses 21 and 24) pledging to serve the LORD — what can be inferred about their commitment?
answers: They accept the covenant's risks knowingly
Their actions contradicted their words and they were not serious
They did not understand Joshua's warnings
challenge.explanation: Repeating the pledge indicates a conscious acceptance of the covenant and its responsibilities despite the warnings.

challenge.question: Who are the 'strange gods' Joshua commands them to put away (verse 23)?
answers: Gods of the Israelite tribes only
Foreign gods and objects of worship of the neighboring nations
Angels and heavenly beings
challenge.explanation: 'Strange gods' refers to foreign deities and idols of the surrounding peoples that must be removed.

challenge.question: The emphasis 'he will not forgive your transgressions nor your sins' (verse 19) reflects which theological trait of the LORD?
answers: Judicial holiness — God as a holy judge who does not ignore sin
That God forgets quickly
That God is indifferent to human conduct
challenge.explanation: The verse highlights God's holiness and judgmental nature: He does not overlook disloyalty and sin.

questions.question: The people's double declarations (verses 21 and 24) pledging to serve the LORD — what can be inferred about their commitment?
answers: They accept the covenant's risks knowingly
Their actions contradicted their words and they were not serious
They did not understand Joshua's warnings
questions.explanation: Repeating the pledge indicates a conscious acceptance of the covenant and its responsibilities despite the warnings.

questions.question: Who are the 'strange gods' Joshua commands them to put away (verse 23)?
answers: Gods of the Israelite tribes only
Foreign gods and objects of worship of the neighboring nations
Angels and heavenly beings
questions.explanation: 'Strange gods' refers to foreign deities and idols of the surrounding peoples that must be removed.

questions.question: The emphasis 'he will not forgive your transgressions nor your sins' (verse 19) reflects which theological trait of the LORD?
answers: Judicial holiness — God as a holy judge who does not ignore sin
That God forgets quickly
That God is indifferent to human conduct
questions.explanation: The verse highlights God's holiness and judgmental nature: He does not overlook disloyalty and sin.

paragraphs.title: Covenant and the Stone of Witness

easy.question: What did Joshua do 'that day' in verse 25?
answers: Made a covenant with the people
Won a battle against enemies
Divided the land among the tribes
easy.explanation: Verse 25 says 'So Joshua made a covenant with the people that day' — he concluded a covenant.

easy.question: Where did Joshua write the words of the covenant (verse 26)?
answers: In a letter to foreign rulers
In the book of the law of God
On a private papyrus
easy.explanation: Verse 26 states Joshua wrote these words in the book of the law of God.

easy.question: What did Joshua take and set up there (verse 26)?
answers: A bronze statue
A chest with the sacred scrolls
A great stone
easy.explanation: The verse says he 'took a great stone and set it up there'.

medium.question: What does 'witness' mean in the phrase 'this stone shall be a witness unto us'?
answers: A sleeping place
A public testimony or proof
A document seal
medium.explanation: Here 'witness' means a public sign or testimony that the stone will testify to the words spoken.

medium.question: Why did Joshua write these words in the book of the law of the LORD, according to the context?
answers: To send the text to foreign tribes
To officially record the covenant and what was said
To hide the words from the people
medium.explanation: Writing in the book of the law was meant to officially document the covenant and the words declared that day.

medium.question: Where was the stone set up according to verse 26?
answers: On top of a hill near water
At the center of the camp of the tribes
Under the oak that was by the sanctuary of the LORD
medium.explanation: Verse 26 specifies the stone was set up under the oak that was by the sanctuary of the LORD.

challenge.question: What is meant by 'lest ye deny your God' in verse 27 (context: the stone as witness)?
answers: You might forget your place in the land
You might deny or renounce your faith and the covenant with God
You might worship both God and other gods simultaneously
challenge.explanation: The stone serves as a witness so they will not deny God's covenant or renounce His sovereignty.

challenge.question: Why was using a stone as a witness significant in the ancient Near East?
answers: Stones were used only for burials and not public memory
There was a ban on using stones for cult purposes, so it was insignificant
A stone served as a permanent, public marker — a visible memory that remained in place
challenge.explanation: Stones and standing stones were common public memorials — permanent visual reminders and testimony in the landscape.

challenge.question: What is the difference in emphasis between calling the stone a 'witness' and calling it a 'memorial'?
answers: There is no difference — they mean the same
'Witness' emphasizes public proof for others; 'memorial' emphasizes keeping the event in memory
'Witness' means legal ownership, 'memorial' means ritual sacrifice
challenge.explanation: 'Witness' highlights the stone's role as public testimony; 'memorial' highlights remembering the event.

questions.question: What is meant by 'lest ye deny your God' in verse 27 (context: the stone as witness)?
answers: You might forget your place in the land
You might deny or renounce your faith and the covenant with God
You might worship both God and other gods simultaneously
questions.explanation: The stone serves as a witness so they will not deny God's covenant or renounce His sovereignty.

questions.question: Why was using a stone as a witness significant in the ancient Near East?
answers: Stones were used only for burials and not public memory
There was a ban on using stones for cult purposes, so it was insignificant
A stone served as a permanent, public marker — a visible memory that remained in place
questions.explanation: Stones and standing stones were common public memorials — permanent visual reminders and testimony in the landscape.

questions.question: What is the difference in emphasis between calling the stone a 'witness' and calling it a 'memorial'?
answers: There is no difference — they mean the same
'Witness' emphasizes public proof for others; 'memorial' emphasizes keeping the event in memory
'Witness' means legal ownership, 'memorial' means ritual sacrifice
questions.explanation: 'Witness' highlights the stone's role as public testimony; 'memorial' highlights remembering the event.

paragraphs.title: Allocation of Inheritance and Joshua's Death

easy.question: What did Joshua do to the people in verse 28?
answers: Sent every man to his inheritance
Ordered them not to travel
Made them priests
easy.explanation: Verse 28 states 'So Joshua let the people depart, every man unto his inheritance' — he sent each to his allotted land.

easy.question: When is Joshua's death said to have occurred according to verse 29?
answers: Before the events described
After these things
During the campaign of conquest
easy.explanation: Verse 29 begins 'And it came to pass after these things that Joshua... died' — he died after the events described.

easy.question: How old was Joshua when he died according to verse 29?
answers: One hundred years
Ninety years
One hundred and ten years
easy.explanation: The verse records Joshua died at the age of one hundred and ten years.

medium.question: Where was Joshua buried according to verse 30?
answers: In a valley near the Jordan
In a city by the sea
In Timnathserah in mount Ephraim, on the north side of the hill of Gaash
medium.explanation: Verse 30 specifies Joshua was buried in Timnathserah in mount Ephraim, north of the hill of Gaash.

medium.question: What does the word 'inheritance' mean in the context 'every man unto his inheritance'?
answers: A parcel of land assigned to him
A personal name
A punishment or period of forced labor
medium.explanation: 'Inheritance' here refers to the land allotment or portion assigned to each man.

medium.question: What is the chronological order of events in verses 28–30?
answers: He died, then sent the people, then was buried
He sent the people to their inheritances, then died, then was buried
They buried him, then he died, then the people were sent
medium.explanation: The sequence is: Joshua sent the people to their inheritances (v.28), then he died (v.29), and then he was buried (v.30).

challenge.question: What does 'in the border of his inheritance' (v.30) suggest about Joshua's relation to the place of his burial?
answers: He died without a known burial place
He was buried in land belonging to a foreign kingdom
He was buried within his own allotted inheritance, i.e., his share of the land
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates Joshua was buried within the boundaries of his allotted inheritance — his own portion of the land.

challenge.question: How does verse 30 describe Timnathserah's position relative to the hill of Gaash?
answers: South of the hill of Gaash
North of the hill of Gaash
East of the hill of Gaash
challenge.explanation: The verse says Timnathserah is in mount Ephraim 'on the north side of the hill of Gaash'.

challenge.question: How does the verse describe Joshua's spiritual or official standing?
answers: As 'the servant of the LORD' — a servant of God
As a dominant reigning king
As an ordinary man with no religious title
challenge.explanation: Joshua is called 'the servant of the LORD', a title denoting his devoted service to God.

questions.question: What does 'in the border of his inheritance' (v.30) suggest about Joshua's relation to the place of his burial?
answers: He died without a known burial place
He was buried in land belonging to a foreign kingdom
He was buried within his own allotted inheritance, i.e., his share of the land
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates Joshua was buried within the boundaries of his allotted inheritance — his own portion of the land.

questions.question: How does verse 30 describe Timnathserah's position relative to the hill of Gaash?
answers: South of the hill of Gaash
North of the hill of Gaash
East of the hill of Gaash
questions.explanation: The verse says Timnathserah is in mount Ephraim 'on the north side of the hill of Gaash'.

questions.question: How does the verse describe Joshua's spiritual or official standing?
answers: As 'the servant of the LORD' — a servant of God
As a dominant reigning king
As an ordinary man with no religious title
questions.explanation: Joshua is called 'the servant of the LORD', a title denoting his devoted service to God.

easy.question: Whom did Israel serve according to the verse?
answers: The LORD
The local kings
Only the priests
easy.explanation: The verse says 'Israel served the LORD' — they worshiped the LORD.

easy.question: When did Israel serve the LORD according to the verse?
answers: Only during battles
All the days of Joshua
Only after Joshua's death
easy.explanation: The verse states 'all the days of Joshua' — indicating the duration of their service during Joshua's lifetime.

easy.question: Who are described as 'those that had known all the works of the LORD' in the verse?
answers: The priests
Joshua himself
The elders
easy.explanation: The verse refers to elders who survived Joshua and who knew the works the LORD had done for Israel.

medium.question: What does the phrase 'and all the days of the elders that overlived Joshua' indicate about the continuity of worship?
answers: That worship ceased after Joshua's death
That the worship of the LORD continued into the elders' generation after Joshua
That the elders separated worship from public life
medium.explanation: It indicates the worship and remembrance of the LORD continued under the elders who lived after Joshua.

medium.question: What does the word 'overlived' mean in 'the elders that overlived Joshua'?
answers: Had their days shortened
Lived many days after Joshua (outlived him)
Extended their official terms
medium.explanation: 'Overlived' means they lived on after the death of Joshua — they outlived him.

medium.question: What does 'all the works of the LORD which he had done for Israel' refer to in the verse?
answers: All the miracles and acts God did for the people
Only a selected set of deeds
Things the Israelites did for themselves
medium.explanation: It refers to the miracles and mighty deeds God performed for Israel, such as the Exodus and conquests.

challenge.question: How does the fact that the elders 'knew' the works of the LORD help preserve national tradition?
answers: It only served to boast about victories
They transmitted memories and lessons to later generations
They wrote new unrelated laws
challenge.explanation: Elders who experienced and knew God's deeds could pass on stories and lessons to preserve communal memory and identity.

challenge.question: The verse mentions both 'all the days of Joshua' and 'all the days of the elders that overlived Joshua' — what does this suggest about time?
answers: The periods are unrelated
The elders acted before Joshua
There is continuity between Joshua's era and the elders' era
challenge.explanation: The pairing emphasizes continuity: the pattern of worship under Joshua carried on into the elders' generation.

challenge.question: In the context of Joshua, what does the verb 'served' include?
answers: Worship, covenant observance and obedience to the LORD
Only physical work on the temple construction
Only agricultural labor and tribute
